newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Attempts to block former prime minister Anand Panyarachun's entry into the Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDA) appear to gain momentum when several members of the ruling New Aspiration Party vow to spurn him when Parliament elects CDA members tomorrow. The anti-Anand campaign also involves prominent names in the Chart Thai and Social Action parties and probably the entire Prachakorn Thai Party. (THE NATION)

- Efforts to set up the much-touted administrative court have received an early setback when the cabinet failed to agree which government agency should oversee the new body. Further negotiations are to take place with Minister Pokin Polakul of the Prime Minister's Office, the main architect of the bill, and cabinet secretary-general Visanu Krua-ngarm who want the Council of State to oversee the planned court on side. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Thousands of Hmong living at a Buddhist temple in Saraburi province have been blamed for exacerbating local unemployment problems and have been implicated in a wave of crime involving vice and narcotics. Officials say the Hmong are taking jobs because they are prepared to work for lower wages. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thai Airways International (THAI) has appointed Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Transport and Communications Mahidol Chantrangkun as its new chairman. The decision was made during a shareholder's meeting yesterday. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Bank of Thailand plans to encourage state-run Krung Thai Bank and special-purpose financial institutions to take up to 35 per cent in the failed Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC), while at least two privately-owned commercial banks are reported to be interested in acquiring significant stakes in BBC. Anew round of bidding for BBC will be called early next year. (THE NATION) - The Cabinet has ordered relevant ministries to formulate a cost-cutting package for the petrochemical industry, which will be hurt by lower tariffs from January 1.
